predictions.reasoning:
We are to check whether the context guarantees that ‘If Arlette is omnipresent, then she can guide all.’ Symbolize: O → G.

Given statements:
1. ¬S (Arlette does not sustain nature)
2. H (Arlette maintains harmony)
3. P (Arlette hears prayers)
4. B (Arlette brings balance to the universe)
5. S or N (Arlette either sustains nature or nurtures life)
Since ¬S, from (5) we must have N (Arlette nurtures life)
6. If (N and H) or (¬N and ¬H), then ¬A (where A = Arlette protects all)
We have both N and H, so (N and H) is true, so by (6) we get ¬A
7. P ⊕ V (Arlette either hears prayers or sees all, but not both)
We have P, so ¬V (Arlette does not see all)
8. If ¬A, then ¬V and ¬G
We already have ¬A, so (8) yields ¬V and ¬G (Arlette cannot guide all)
9. B ⊕ U (Arlette either brings balance to the universe or heals souls, but not both)
We have B, so ¬U (Arlette does not heal souls)
10. O or U (Arlette is either omnipresent or heals souls)
Since ¬U, (10) forces O (Arlette is omnipresent)

Therefore we now know:
Arlette is omnipresent (O is true).
Arlette cannot guide all (G is false).

So we have an instance where O is true but G is false, falsifying the conditional O → G.
Hence the context does not entail the conclusion; it actually falsifies it.
